keyTerms.definition: Shape, then method and results, then a virtual reimplementation.
Read in the order listed; each one builds on the last.

recall.question: What does each chapter cover?
recall.answer: The problem, the key idea from zero, the core math with real numbers, why it mattered, what came next.

sections.title: Paper 1: Attention Is All You Need (2017)

keyTerms.definition: Vaswani et al., NeurIPS 2017; the root of the spine.
NeurIPS 2017; Google Brain, Toronto.
What sequence models were before 2017: sequential, hard to parallelize.

recall.question: Why is this the root?
recall.answer: It builds on nothing earlier in the volume; Volume 4 taught the transformer mechanically.

keyTerms.definition: Su et al., 2021; rotary position embedding.
The literature RoPE tuning created.

recall.question: What came after RoPE?
recall.answer: ALiBi, position interpolation, NTK-aware scaling, YaRN, 128k-context models.

sections.title: Paper 3: FlashAttention, Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness (2022)

keyTerms.definition: Dao et al., 2022; fast, memory-efficient, exact attention with IO-awareness.
Attention as a design discipline.

recall.question: What followed FlashAttention?
recall.answer: FA-2 and 3, FlashDecoding, FlexAttention, RingAttention for million-token context.

sections.title: Paper 4: GPT-2, Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners (2019)

keyTerms.definition: Radford et al., OpenAI, 2019; language models are unsupervised multitask learners.
The paper; the era it ended.

recall.question: What era ended after GPT-2?
recall.answer: The 'spicy autocomplete' era; T5, GPT-3, scaling laws, Chinchilla, LLaMA followed.

sections.title: Paper 5: GPT-3, Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (2020)

keyTerms.definition: Brown et al., NeurIPS 2020; language models are few-shot learners.
OpenAI; the three settings in Section 2.

recall.question: What did GPT-3 make real?
recall.answer: Few-shot learning; prompting works, then chain-of-thought, InstructGPT, RLHF.

sections.title: Paper 6: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models, Kaplan et al. (2020)

keyTerms.definition: Kaplan et al., OpenAI, 2020; how loss scales with compute, data, size.
The paper’s identifier.

sections.title: Paper 7: Chinchilla, Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (2022)

keyTerms.definition: Hoffmann et al., DeepMind, 2022; training compute-optimal LLMs; the 70B model.
The split Chinchilla corrected.

recall.question: What did LLaMA 13B prove?
recall.answer: On 1T tokens it beats 175B GPT-3; small models trained long.

sections.title: Paper 8: InstructGPT, Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback (2022)

keyTerms.definition: Ouyang et al., NeurIPS 2022; training models to follow instructions with human feedback.
Reinforcement learning from human feedback.

recall.question: What came after InstructGPT?
recall.answer: ChatGPT, Constitutional AI, DPO, RLAIF, DeepSeek-R1, reasoning models.

sections.title: Paper 9: Constitutional AI, Harmlessness from AI Feedback (2022)

keyTerms.definition: Bai et al., Anthropic, 2022; harmlessness from AI feedback.
Instead of labels.

recall.question: What lineage followed?
recall.answer: Claude ships it; collective CAI, deliberative alignment, interpretability.

keyTerms.definition: Rafailov et al., NeurIPS 2023; the model is secretly a reward model.
The paper’s identifier.

recall.question: What variants followed DPO?
recall.answer: IPO, KTO, ORPO, online DPO, RLVR, reward-hacking studies.

sections.title: Paper 11: LLaMA, Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models (2023)

keyTerms.definition: Touvron et al., Meta AI, 2023; open and efficient; 7B to 65B.
The paper’s identifier.

recall.question: What did the open ecosystem do?
recall.answer: Alpaca, Vicuna, LoRA/QLoRA, LLaMA 2, Mistral and Mixtral, LLaMA 3, open DeepSeek.

sections.title: Paper 12: Mixtral of Experts, Sparse Mixture of Experts (2024)

keyTerms.definition: Jiang et al., Mistral AI, 2024; sparse mixture of experts.
The SMoE idea goes back to 2017's 'Outrageously Large Neural Networks'.

recall.question: What followed Mixtral?
recall.answer: Switch Transformer, DeepSeekMoE, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen MoE, sparse hardware.

sections.title: Paper 13: RAG (2020) and ReAct (2022), Grounding and Agency

keyTerms.definition: Lewis et al., 2020; retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-intensive tasks.
Yao et al., 2022; synergizing reasoning and acting.

recall.question: What is the debate?
recall.answer: RAG versus long context; million-token windows compete with retrieval.

sections.title: Paper 14: DeepSeek-R1 (2025), Reasoning from Verifiable Rewards

keyTerms.definition: DeepSeek-AI, 2025; incentivizing reasoning via RL; arXiv:2501.12948.
Pure RL in Section 2.

recall.question: What is the new paradigm?
recall.answer: Verifiable rewards; the default for math and code.

sections.title: Synthesis: How the Fourteen Papers Connect

keyTerms.definition: Foundation, science of scale, alignment, modern open.
Redraw the spine from memory.

recall.question: What are the four acts?
recall.answer: Act 1: papers 1-5 (foundation). Act 2: 6-7 (scale). Act 3: 8-10 (alignment). Act 4: modern open.

keyTerms.definition: Grouped by which spine paper they extend; read with the spine paper in hand.
Attention, scaling, alignment, reasoning, agents, efficiency.

sections.title: Capstone Lab: Replicate a Scaling Law at Tiny Scale

keyTerms.definition: Repeat the measurement on a laptop; feel the exponents.
A reconstruction sketched for this volume, not a paper reproduction.

recall.question: Where did Act 2 come from?
recall.answer: Measurement, not theory; the power law stops being a slogan.

keyTerms.definition: Transformers and attention step-by-step; the visual foundation.
Building GPT by hand.
